title: Getting Arvell Shaw into the Armstrong band
summary: In St. Louis, when the bassist left, Moore recommended Arvell Shaw, and his uncle and aunt visited the Plantation to hear him.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Arvell Shaw was on those sessions. This is, of course, 1946 and what kind of relationship did you have with Arvell?
Arvell -- I think we covered this before when I got in the Armstrong band?
We talked about it but not with the tape.
Well, when we were in St. Louis, Uncle Bill and Aunt Mary knew I was with Armstrong and they were on their way to Arizona to visit and we timed our connection there at St. Louis because the Armstrong

band was going to play The Plantation and so that night they had arrived in time to come to the Club to hear the band and myself and I did my solo on "Stardust" and then afterwards my uncle went back stage and met all the boys and met Louie and talked about Blue Island, when I was a kid there and then that same night the bass player had to leave a few days to go back to Philadelphia, I think it was Al Moore. So Joe Garland asked me, "You've been here before with Jeter-Pillars, do you know a good bass player in town? We need a bass player right away." So I said I know Arvell Shaw, he lives in St. Louis. So the band left and Al had to go back to Philadelphia. I put Arvell Shaw in with Louis. Now to this day I don't know what Arvell would be doing if I hadn't gotten him out of St. Louis.
How did you come in contact with him? How did you know about his musical ability?

Well, being in St. Louis with Jeter-Pillars, we had our own bass player but I've always known Arvell because he'd be in some of the sessions. He played with all the bands around St. Louis, he had a big reputation. He's a good bass player. So when the Armstrong band needed a bass player, I put Arvell Shaw in there.
